title: Zutty Singleton and the Shaw 'Blues' sides with the 25-inch cymbal
summary: Leeman knew Zutty from 1936 and shows his influence on the Shaw 'A and B Blues' record, where he used the giant Chinese cymbal that sold out Bill Mather's shop.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Zutty and I were close and dear friends. I knew him from 1936 until his death in the '70's, which his work rubbed off on me and it influenced my work in that particular era, and it was especially predominant in the Artie Shaw record which was Blues A and Blues B, a collector's item now -- it was double sided, 78, and I think it was a Columbia recording, but I'm not sure. But I think you will hear all of their influences in my playing on these sides -- at that time, before I had changed to what was my present day style, and in addition, my employing on that record 'A and B Blues', the giant 25-inch Chinese cymbal that I started using frequently throughout which caused an influx on sold out Chinese cymbals at Bill Mather's Drum Shop in New York -- the interested jazz buffs and drummers bought them.
